name: Contextual Embedding Variance
description: Measures the variance of contextual word embeddings (e.g., from BERT) to detect the low intra-sentence deviation characteristic of autoregressive AI models.
algorithm: Transformer Embedding Extraction & Vector Variance Profiling
mechanism: Autoregressive LLMs generate text by constantly predicting the most statistically probable next token based on the preceding context window. Because they are mathematically bound to maximize likelihood, the resulting sentences maintain a tight, highly predictable semantic trajectory. If you plot the contextual embeddings (vector representations) of the words in an AI-generated sentence, they cluster tightly together with very low variance from the running average. Human writers, conversely, do not operate via next-token prediction. They frequently pull from diverse cognitive schemas, introducing novel metaphors, sudden topic shifts, or stylistically surprising vocabulary in the middle of a sentence, which causes drastic spikes and high variance in the embedding vectors. This method calculates the mathematical variance of these contextual embeddings; an unnaturally smooth, low-variance trajectory strongly flags synthetic, probability-bound generation.
useCase: Detecting high-quality synthetic text that bypasses surface-level grammatical checks by analyzing the deep mathematical relationships between words as perceived by Transformer models.
strengths:
• Analyzes the fundamental mathematical mechanism of LLM text generation (probability distribution), making it extremely robust against clever prompting or parameter tweaking.
• Highly effective regardless of the topic, genre, or specific vocabulary used.
• Operates on absolute mathematical vector logic rather than subjective stylistic rules.
limitations:
• Computationally expensive; requires loading a heavy encoder model (like BERT or RoBERTa) to extract the contextual embeddings in real-time.
• May trigger false positives on highly formulaic human text, such as boilerplate legal contracts or repetitive technical manuals.
• Requires texts of at least a paragraph in length to establish a statistically significant variance mathematical profile.
parameters:
Analysis: Vector Embedding Extraction & Nearest Neighbor Distance
Metric: Intra-Sentence Contextual Embedding Standard Deviation
Output: 0-100 Synthetic Trajectory (Low Variance) Score
accuracy: High — 85-90%. One of the most academically rigorous detection methods available. Highly resilient to simple evasion techniques like synonym swapping.

references.title: Devlin, J. et al. (2019). BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers. NAACL.
Tulchinskii, E. et al. (2023). Intrinsic Dimension Estimation for Robust Detection of AI-Generated Texts. NeurIPS.
